# Engineering Standards

The doctrine this codebase is reviewed against — the durable rules, distilled
from the normative design in [`docs/SPEC.md`](../docs/SPEC.md) and the
per-change rationale in [`docs/learnings/`](../docs/learnings/).
`CONTRIBUTING.md` covers *who* may change what; this file covers *how* changes
must behave. Inherited from `workout-logger` (`.github/STANDARDS.md` at
`5bffddfb80fc`) and rewritten for this app.

## Architecture

- **Local-first.** On-device SQLite is the single source of truth. No server,
  no account, no cloud sync operated by us.
- **One write path.** All SQL lives in `RecipeToGroceryList/Storage/`. A recipe
  lands through `RecipeStore.save(_ draft:)` and nowhere else
  (`RecipeDraft → RecipeValidator.validate → transaction → save`); selection,
  check-off and manual items go through their typed store methods. Feature code
  never runs ad hoc SQL, never touches `store.db`, and never constructs a
  `SQLiteDB` — `scripts/check_store_boundary.sh` fails CI if it does.
  `SQLiteDB.transaction` does not nest.
- **Model proposes, app confirms, app writes.** Output from the on-device LLM,
  the fuzzy layer, the embedding layer and OCR is a *proposal*. Nothing lands
  without the user tapping Save, and no layer below the store ever writes an
  alias or an ingredient — alias and ingredient creation happen inside `save`.
- **Per-row results, never all-or-nothing.** A line the model or the splitter
  cannot read becomes a visible *unresolved* row in Confirm. It is never a reason
  to discard the other fourteen lines (the workout app's whole-entry decline is
  deliberately *not* inherited).
- **No clarification loop.** The parse outcome is `draft | declined`. Low
  confidence is surfaced as a highlighted or *New* row in the Confirm UI, which
  is the clarification step; the app does not ask the model follow-up questions.
- **The list is computed.** The grocery list is a pure function of
  `(selected recipes, manual items, check_state)` — `GroceryListBuilder.build`.
  There is no persisted list table and no cached rows; check state lives on the
  canonical ingredient and is garbage-collected in the same transaction as the
  selection change that orphaned it.
- **Concurrency discipline.** Writes are `@MainActor`-gated; off-main reads go
  through `SQLiteDB.readTransaction` (serialized on the connection lock), and
  multi-read consumers use `RecipeStore.snapshot` for a consistent view.
  FULLMUTEX alone is not an argument that a multi-statement closure is safe.
- **Gated frameworks stay in one file each.** `FoundationModels` symbols only in
  `Parsing/FoundationRecipeParser.swift` (whole file inside
  `#if canImport(FoundationModels)`), `Vision` only in
  `Vision/VisionTextRecognizer.swift`, `NaturalLanguage` only in
  `Model/NLContextualEmbeddingIngredientMatcher.swift`. Factories are the only
  `#if` meeting points. Every feature works when the refiner is `nil`.

## Data honesty

- **Never invent a number.** The splitter and the model may only report a
  quantity the line states; a model quantity where the regex found none is
  dropped. No unit conversion, ever. Amounts are summed only when every
  contributing line has a quantity and the same `unit_key`; otherwise the lines
  are shown and no total is.
- **Nothing silently dropped.** Every raw line the user gave us is kept
  verbatim in `recipes.raw_lines`, and `recipe_ingredients.raw_line` is never
  edited. Canonicalization is additive: *Keep as text* is how a line survives
  without a guess.
- **Aliases have one owner.** `ingredient_aliases.alias` is the PRIMARY KEY, so
  an ambiguous term cannot map to two canonicals; the tap that would create the
  conflict is refused with "*X* already means *Y*", never resolved by a layer.
- **Bundled data is built, not hand-edited.** `seed_ingredients.json` is
  generated by `scripts/build_seed.py` from `scripts/seed_source.json` (the
  hand-authored, CC0 source of record); CI fails if the two disagree.

## Privacy

- **The privacy sentences live in four places and the site is canonical:**
  https://lukefwalton.com/recipe-to-grocery-list/privacy/ first, then
  `docs/privacy.md`, the in-app Privacy screen (`PrivacyCopy` in
  `Features/Settings/PrivacyView.swift`) and the App Store listing
  (`docs/app-store-metadata.md`). An edit to any one of them is an edit to all
  four, in that order, in one PR. lukefwalton.com is the source of truth for
  everything public-facing (privacy, support, terms if they ever exist).
- Claims in UI copy, `docs/privacy.md`, the App Store privacy label and the
  README must describe the same product, in the same words. The fetch policy is
  one sentence everywhere: *"When you give it a link, the app downloads that
  page, once, and nothing else."* Any change to `Import/RecipeFetchPolicy.swift`
  updates that sentence — or proves it still holds — in the same PR.
- The wording for the LLM is "no **cloud** AI" — the optional parser uses
  Apple's on-device model, and no line ever leaves the device.
- The App Group exists only for the Share Extension's one-way inbox. The
  extension never opens the database; the database never leaves the app
  sandbox.
- Photos are processed in memory and never stored. Camera and photo permission
  are requested in context, never at launch.
- No analytics, no telemetry, no crash reporter, no third-party SDKs. New
  entitlements or permissions require explicit opt-in UX and a privacy-policy
  update in the same change.

## Schema & compatibility

- Schema changes ship with a `Schema.migrate` step (forward-only on
  `PRAGMA user_version`) and tests; constraints that protect the data contract
  (CHECKs on closed vocabularies, UNIQUE slugs, the alias PRIMARY KEY, FK
  cascades) live in the schema itself, not just in Swift.
- Swift enums that mirror a schema CHECK (`IngredientCategory`, `SourceKind`,
  `RowResolution`) use the schema's raw values verbatim, so the two can never
  disagree.

## Testing & CI

- Behavior that protects an invariant gets a test at the right altitude —
  connection/schema guarantees in `SQLiteDBTests`, store semantics in
  `RecipeStoreTests`, pure functions (splitter, normalizer, fuzzy, list builder,
  model mapping) in their own files. UI-only styling does not need tests.
- Tests never need the network, Vision, NaturalLanguage or Foundation Models.
  Fixtures (`ingredient_lines.json`, saved HTML) are bundled and loaded offline.
- The golden corpus pass rate is printed (`[GoldenCorpus] …`) and asserted
  against the baseline stored in the fixture; a drop fails the build.
- Conditional compilation must be provable in CI. Anything behind
  `#if canImport(...)` needs a job where the branch actually compiles (see
  `foundation-models-guard` in `ios-tests.yml`) — a green build on a toolchain
  without the SDK proves only the fallback.

## Design

- `lfwdesignsystem/` is edited in `a-new-word-every-day` only, then synced;
  `check_designsystem_sync.sh` guards the copy. Colors come from `LFWColors` and
  palette tokens; status is `success` / `warning` / `danger`, never system
  `.red` / `.green` / `.orange`.
- Type by role: Fraunces (`.uiTitle`) for recipe titles, ingredient headings and
  empty-state titles; Inter for everything else; numerals always Inter. The
  typeface picker offers only `Theme.bundledTypefaces`.

## Code shape

- Zero third-party dependencies. A small published algorithm (Jaro–Winkler,
  fraction parsing, JSON-LD walking) is re-implemented with attribution in the
  file and in `NOTICE.md`, never vendored as a package.
- Files stay navigable: one type may span multiple focused files
  (`RecipeStore+*.swift`), and a file trending past ~1,000 lines is a signal to
  find the next extraction boundary, not to keep appending.
- Comments record *why* (the constraint or trade-off), not *what*, and cite the
  sibling file and revision when a pattern was inherited
  (`workout-logger@5bffddfb80fc`, `a-new-word-every-day@e829bcc9c0dc`).
  Significant decisions get a `docs/learnings/` entry in the same PR.
